events.headline: Anthropic founded by ex-OpenAI researchers led by the Amodeis
events.summary: Anthropic was founded at the beginning of 2021 (Delaware entity date January 26, 2021) by former OpenAI staff, with Dario Amodei as CEO and Daniela Amodei as President, alongside co-founders Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Tom Brown, Chris Olah, Sam McCandlish and Ben Mann.

source.title: Anthropic raises Series B to build robust AI

extracted.governance: Founded as a public benefit corporation; mission framed as AI safety and research ('steerable, interpretable, robust' systems).
extracted.moat: Founding team wrote the GPT-3 and scaling-laws work at OpenAI (per Core Views page).
extracted.strategy: Initially research-first; commercialization 'down the road' (TechCrunch, May 2021).

events.notes: Anthropic's own T1 text says only 'founding at the beginning of 2021'; the Jan 26, 2021 date comes from a T4 SAM.gov-derived profile (cited by Wikipedia). Founder list is from T4 sources (Wikipedia citing CNBC 2025 and Reuters 2023, which I could not open); Anthropic sometimes describes seven co-founders. Contrary Research says 'December 2020' and that 15 researchers left OpenAI — see conflicts.

events.headline: Incorporated as Delaware public benefit corporation with stated public benefit
events.summary: Anthropic incorporated in Delaware as a Public Benefit Corporation whose 2021 charter states the specific public benefit as 'to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the cultural, social and technological improvement of humanity' (later reworded to 'long term benefit of humanity').

source.title: The Long-Term Benefit Trust

corroboration.publisher: Simon Willison (quoting Delaware certificate of incorporation)

extracted.governance: Delaware PBC: directors may balance stockholder financial interests against the charter's public benefit purpose (Anthropic LTBT post). Earliest (2021) charter purpose: 'responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the cultural, social and technological improvement of humanity'; later versions: 'for the long term benefit of humanity'.

other.charter_language_source: Delaware certificates of incorporation folder linked from Simon Willison post (not opened directly)

events.notes: PBC status is T1-confirmed (Anthropic LTBT post, Series A page footer, company page). The exact 2021 charter wording is quoted by a T4 blog from Delaware filings I could not open; date of the original certificate assumed equal to the entity date (Jan 26, 2021).

events.headline: Series A: $124M led by Jaan Tallinn
events.summary: Anthropic announced a $124 million Series A led by Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn with James McClave, Dustin Moskovitz, the Center for Emerging Risk Research and Eric Schmidt, to fund computationally intensive research on steerable, interpretable and robust large-scale AI systems.

source.title: Anthropic raises $124 million to build more reliable, general AI systems

extracted.governance: Round backed almost entirely by tech founders/philanthropists rather than institutional VCs; Series A documents also created the 'Long-Term Benefit Committee' (see evt-20210528-ltb-committee).
extracted.strategy: Use of proceeds: research roadmap and prototypes of reliable, steerable AI; 'primarily focused on research' with commercial value 'down the road' (TechCrunch).

other.dealroom_estimate_basis: Forge Global secondary data; 'Anthropic never confirmed the figure'

events.notes: Round size $124M confirmed by T1 + T2. Valuation was not disclosed; Dealroom's $623M post-money is an unconfirmed secondary-market estimate. Dealroom's own round-size figures ($80.2M/$90.9M) diverge from the announced total — recorded in conflicts as a likely tranche-accounting artifact.

events.headline: Series A documents create 'Long-Term Benefit Committee', LTBT precursor
events.summary: An earlier version of the Long-Term Benefit Trust, called the Long-Term Benefit Committee, was written into Anthropic's 2021 Series A documents, the origin of the governance mechanism later formalized (with Class T stock) at the Series C.

source.title: The Long-Term Benefit Trust

extracted.governance: LTBT lineage: 'Long-Term Benefit Committee' in 2021 Series A docs -> Long-Term Benefit Trust formalized at Series C via amended charter creating Class T stock that elects/removes directors on time- and funding-based milestones (majority of board within 4 years).

events.notes: Anthropic states the committee was in the 2021 Series A documents; exact execution date not given, so dated to the Series A announcement month. Formal LTBT announcement (Sept 19, 2023) is out of this scout's period.

events.headline: First alignment paper: 'General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment'
events.summary: Anthropic's first major alignment paper (Askell et al., 22 authors, arXiv 2112.00861) framed the 'helpful, honest, harmless' assistant as a testbed and found ranked preference modeling scales better than imitation learning.

source.title: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment

extracted.moat: Establishes the HHH (helpful/honest/harmless) framing that underpins Claude's later training.

events.headline: Publishes 'A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits'
events.summary: Anthropic's interpretability team (Elhage, Nanda, Olsson et al., 25 authors) published the foundational mechanistic-interpretability framework for reverse-engineering attention-only transformers and identified 'induction heads'.

source.title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits

extracted.moat: Mechanistic interpretability program led by co-founder Chris Olah; author list (25 names incl. all founders) is a proxy for the research staff at end-2021.

events.headline: 'Predictability and Surprise' policy paper, later presented at FAccT '22
events.summary: Ganguli et al. (30 authors, arXiv 2202.07785) argued that large generative models combine predictable scaling-law loss with unpredictable specific capabilities, framing Anthropic's policy case for pre-deployment evaluation; accepted to ACM FAccT '22.

source.title: Predictability and Surprise in Large Generative Models

extracted.strategy: Positions Anthropic as a policy voice on emergent-capability risk; ties to Jack Clark's 2022 government engagements.

events.headline: 'In-context Learning and Induction Heads' interpretability result
events.summary: Anthropic published research arguing that induction heads are the circuit mechanism behind in-context learning in transformers, extending the December 2021 framework.

source.title: In-context learning and induction heads

events.notes: Author list not shown on the anthropic.com summary page.

events.headline: RLHF 'helpful and harmless assistant' paper released
events.summary: Bai et al. (31 authors, arXiv 2204.05862) applied preference modeling and reinforcement learning from human feedback to train a helpful and harmless assistant, finding alignment training improved almost all NLP evaluations — the technical basis of Claude's training.

source.title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

extracted.moat: Core RLHF recipe (with the accompanying HH-RLHF dataset) used for Claude.

events.headline: Jack Clark appointed to inaugural National AI Advisory Committee
events.summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce named Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark one of 27 inaugural members of the National AI Advisory Committee (NAIAC), which advises the President under the National AI Initiative Act of 2020.

source.title: U.S. Department of Commerce Appoints 27 Members to National AI Advisory Committee

extracted.strategy: Early federal policy access: Anthropic seated alongside Google (James Manyika, vice chair), Microsoft (Ashley Llorens), AWS (Swami Sivasubramanian), IBM (Christina Montgomery) and NVIDIA (Keith Strier); OpenAI not represented.

events.notes: Commerce.gov version of the release returned 403; NIST mirror opened.

events.headline: Series B: $580M led by Sam Bankman-Fried; ~40 staff
events.summary: Anthropic announced a $580 million Series B led by FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried (~$500 million of it, per DOJ) with Caroline Ellison, Jim McClave, Nishad Singh, Jaan Tallinn and the Center for Emerging Risk Research, to build large-scale experimental infrastructure for safety research, at a time when the company had about 40 employees in San Francisco.

source.title: Anthropic raises Series B to build robust AI

corroboration.publisher: U.S. DOJ letter, US v. Bankman-Fried, S6 22 Cr. 673 (LAK), Dkt. 315 (CourtListener)

compute.term: Use of proceeds: 'large-scale experimental infrastructure' for computationally intensive models

extracted.governance: Daniela Amodei: 'focusing on ensuring Anthropic has the culture and governance to continue to responsibly explore and develop safe AI systems as we scale.' Investor set again non-institutional (FTX/Alameda principals + Series A backers).
extracted.strategy: Dario Amodei: explore predictable scaling properties while examining unpredictable emergence of capabilities and safety issues at scale.

other.sbf_component_source: DOJ Dkt. 315: 'invested approximately $500 million in Anthropic ... in April 2022'

events.notes: Valuation not disclosed by any opened source (aggregators cite ~$4B; unverified — open item). The $500M SBF/Alameda component is from DOJ's Oct 2023 letter and 2024 estate reporting, not from Anthropic. Transaction-date conflict: Protos and AFP date the $500M investment to 2021 (Protos: Oct 5, 2021) vs. April 2022 per Anthropic and DOJ — see conflicts. Dealroom lists the round as $375.3M (likely partial tranche data).

events.headline: First version of Claude trained in spring 2022, withheld from release
events.summary: Anthropic trained the first version of its headline model, Claude, in spring 2022 and chose to prioritize it for internal safety research rather than public deployment, citing race-dynamics concerns.

source.title: Core Views on AI Safety: When, Why, What, and How

extracted.strategy: Deliberate non-release of a frontier-class model in 2022 to avoid accelerating a race; public release came March 2023 (scout-2023).

events.notes: Date precision is seasonal ('spring 2022' per Anthropic); Wikipedia says training finished 'summer 2022' — recorded in conflicts. Date field is a placeholder for Q2 2022. Model-size claims not verified.

events.headline: 'Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know' calibration paper
events.summary: Kadavath et al. (36 authors, arXiv 2207.05221) showed language models can assess the reliability of their own answers, part of Anthropic's honesty research line.

source.title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know

events.headline: Red-teaming paper releases 38,961-attack dataset
events.summary: Ganguli et al. (36 authors, arXiv 2209.07858) red-teamed models across sizes, found RLHF models get harder to red-team as they scale, and released a dataset of 38,961 red-team attacks.

source.title: Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned

events.headline: 'Toy Models of Superposition' interpretability paper
events.summary: Elhage et al. (16 authors, arXiv 2209.10652) showed how networks store more features than neurons via superposition, explaining polysemanticity — groundwork for later dictionary-learning interpretability.

source.title: Toy Models of Superposition

events.headline: Jack Clark testifies before Senate Commerce Committee on AI
events.summary: Anthropic's Head of Policy Jack Clark submitted written testimony to a U.S. Senate Commerce Committee hearing on emerging technologies, urging government measurement/evaluation capacity for AI, NIST's role in risk frameworks, and tracking of compute used in training.

source.publisher: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
source.title: Written Testimony of Jack Clark (Anthropic), Sept. 29, 2022 hearing

corroboration.publisher: U.S. Senate Commerce Committee (duplicate testimony file)

extracted.strategy: Policy platform: measurement/evaluation infrastructure, NIST funding, compute tracking, AI safety research support.

entities.name: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

events.notes: PDF opened but text extraction was partial; hearing date taken from the committee's file name (2022.09.29, 'CST_EmergingTechHearing'); hearing title and subcommittee not verified. Clark's title rendered as 'Head of Policy'/'Policy Director' across two extractions.

events.headline: 'Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight' paper (Bowman et al.)
events.summary: Bowman et al. (46 authors, arXiv 2211.03540) proposed an experimental framework for humans overseeing stronger AI and showed humans assisted by an unreliable LLM dialog assistant outperform both the model alone and unaided humans.

source.title: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models

people.name: Samuel R. Bowman
people.role: First author (NYU professor working at Anthropic)

events.headline: FTX/Alameda file Chapter 11; Anthropic's lead investor becomes bankruptcy estate
events.summary: FTX Trading, FTX US, Alameda Research and 130+ affiliates filed for Chapter 11 and Sam Bankman-Fried resigned in favor of John J. Ray III, turning the ~$500 million Anthropic Series B stake (later disclosed as 44,539,240 Series B preferred shares) into an estate asset that DOJ would allege was bought with FTX customer deposits.

source.title: FTX files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy; Sam Bankman-Fried resigns

corroboration.publisher: U.S. DOJ letter, US v. Bankman-Fried, Dkt. 315 (CourtListener)

extracted.governance: Largest single shareholder from the Series B enters Chapter 11 seven months after investing; stake later (2024) sold by the estate, mostly to ATIC Third International Investment Co. (Mubadala-linked) — outside this period.

other.stake_pct_reported_by_aggregators: ~8% (BeInCrypto/Yahoo, T4); initial ~13.56% appears only in unopened aggregator snippets

events.notes: The Nov 11, 2022 filing is T2-confirmed; share count/price and 7.84% stake are from Protos citing the estate's Feb 2024 sale filing (not opened directly). No opened Nov-2022 source ties Anthropic to the leaked FTX balance sheet — Fortune and Visual Capitalist coverage of it do not mention Anthropic. Governance rights attached to the FTX shares are unverified.

events.headline: Claude in closed alpha with Notion, Quora, DuckDuckGo, Robin AI
events.summary: In the months before its March 2023 launch, Anthropic ran Claude in a closed alpha with launch partners Notion (writing/summarization in Notion AI), Quora (Poe), DuckDuckGo (DuckAssist), Juni Learning, Robin AI (contract language) and AssemblyAI.

source.title: Introducing Claude

corroboration.publisher: SiliconANGLE (Claude 'available only in closed beta through Slack integration', Feb 3, 2023)

extracted.strategy: Partner-led, API-first go-to-market seeded before public launch; first named customers.
extracted.customers: Notion, Quora/Poe, DuckDuckGo, Juni Learning, Robin AI, AssemblyAI (closed alpha)

events.notes: Timing inferred: Anthropic wrote on Mar 14, 2023 that it had worked with these partners 'for the past few months', i.e. roughly Q4 2022; no opened source gives a start date. Whether Claude was inside Poe's Dec 21, 2022 invite-only beta is unverified (Quora blog returned 403).

events.headline: Constitutional AI paper introduces RLAIF
events.summary: Bai et al. (51 authors, arXiv 2212.08073) introduced Constitutional AI — self-critique/revision plus reinforcement learning from AI feedback guided by a written set of principles — the method Anthropic would market as Claude's differentiator.

source.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

extracted.moat: Proprietary training methodology (CAI/RLAIF) reducing reliance on human harm labels; central to Claude's brand.

events.headline: Model-written evaluations paper flags sycophancy and power-seeking
events.summary: Perez et al. (63 authors, arXiv 2212.09251) auto-generated 154 evaluation datasets and found larger RLHF models show more sycophancy and stated power-seeking/shutdown-avoidance tendencies — Anthropic's first published pre-release sycophancy evaluation of Claude-class models.

source.title: Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations

events.notes: Perez's 2022 join date comes from search-result profiles (OpenReview/FAR.AI) that were not opened.
